`TreeItem::get_child()` also calls `_create_children_cache()` to rebuild the cache. Rebuilding the cache is unavoidable in most cases.

This code snippet will rebuild the cache when moving to a new parent node with no children. Otherwise, the cache may already exist.

`Tree::draw_item()` calls `Tree::get_visible_child_count()`, which usually rebuilds the cache. So the expanded item usually has the cache created/rebuilt.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/aa8d9b83f66488dbb2c9c918e9016ef80f821fb4/scene/gui/tree.cpp#L2615-L2617

If the cache is already created, using `p_parent->get_child_count()` to determine the index is cheaper than using `item->get_index()`. Especially when moving multiple nodes in batches.

But in the "happy case" we don't call TreeItem::get_child() at all. The happy case is:

* Add the node to parent (TreeItem::add_child() does not create a cache)
* Node is already in the right place (TreeItem::get_index() is cheaper than building the cache)

I understand what you are saying, but I don't think that adding the cost of building the cache to the "happy path" is the right choice.

In most cases, we need to see the item before we can operate it. In order to see it, `Tree::draw_item()` is called, which creates the cache. So the cost of creating the cache is not here. In addition to moving to the node that previously had no child nodes.

Someone on one of the discord servers yesterday was asking about why scene operations were slow when they only had a few editable nodes, but many nodes in subscenes, and I linked them this PR but it got me thinking about this case and its generalization again.

In the case of non-editable subscenes, I think renames could result in a different value if either 1) the nodepath has a saved value that references outside of its individual scene tree (and so would always be skipped if renames happened for that scene itself) or 2) a tool script assigns a valid nodepath once the subscene is added to another scene. But in both cases I don't think saving would result in that subscene's packed data being updated for the new path.

In the case of child nodes of nodes being renamed/moved, it would only be safe to skip them if the nodepath change was at a level shared by the node and the node being renamed for all nodes being renamed. So always the case for direct parents/grandparents renames, but not necessarily for a parent's sibling node which might have a name change as well as a parent change on a reparent operation, or in batch renames.
